chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from his father who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have young children with me and I fear the cold for them. From where should they enter the state of Ihram?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Take them to Al-Araj so they may enter Ihram from it, for when you reach Al-Araj, you enter Tihama.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'And if you fear for them, take them to Al-Juhfa.'
ai.seo_question: Where should young children enter the state of Ihram for Hajj if they are afraid of the cold?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of *mubah* (permissibility) and flexibility in applying the rules of Ihram for dependents, prioritizing their physical comfort (*raf' al-haraj*) over rigid adherence to the primary miqat. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical jurisprudence (*fiqh*) where the guardian's judgment regarding the child's well-being determines the validity of the ritual state. The mention of Al-Araj and Al-Juhfa highlights the historical geographical markers used in early Islamic jurisprudence to define the boundaries of the sacred precincts.
